ignored._actionQueues: not captured/restored: RestoreTo only ever runs when ActionQueueSet.IsEmpty is true (UndoProtocol.CommitAsync's gate, background invariant) and restoring game data never enqueues new actions, so every per-player queue (ActionQueueSet.cs:48) is already correctly empty at both capture and restore time
ignored._actionsWaitingForResumption: Change C investigation (see report): entries are transient, decoupled resume-message/pause-call races inherent to normal multiplayer message ordering (ResumeActionWithoutSynchronizing :499-520 queues an entry when TryGetAction fails or the action isn't yet GatheringPlayerChoice; PauseActionForPlayerChoice :270-279 is what consumes it, whenever that action's OWN pause eventually runs) — not model data our undo semantically rewinds, and not reachable through _actionQueues emptiness the way _wasReset is. Deliberately left untouched: clearing it on restore risks discarding a legitimate pending resume for an action that hasn't reached its pause call yet. NOTE: because RestoreTo rewinds _nextId (action ids get reused), a leftover entry whose oldId falls inside the rewound range is a latent collision risk with a future action reusing that id — flagged, not fixed, since we could not prove it is ever actually populated at an idle-queue restore point
